title: Breakthrough Starshot
subtitle: To the stars in 20 years
yt_title: A Plan to Reach Another Star in 20 Years 🚀 | Ep. 68 #shorts
description:
Episode 68 of a daily journey through the universe. 🚀
Breakthrough Starshot, announced in 2016: tiny gram-scale spacecraft on ultra-thin light sails, pushed by powerful lasers to about 20% of the speed of light, could reach Alpha Centauri in about 20 years. The idea, and the huge challenges.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 69: Next stop, the speed of light. The universe's ultimate speed limit.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

segments.text: Episode sixty-eight. Next stop... Breakthrough Starshot.
With today's rockets, reaching Proxima Centauri would take tens of thousands of years.
In twenty sixteen, scientists announced a bold idea to do it in about twenty years. It's called Breakthrough Starshot.
segments.headline: Breakthrough Starshot

segments.text: Instead of one big spaceship, send hundreds of tiny ones. Each would be a chip weighing about a gram.
segments.headline: Tiny spacecraft

segments.text: Each chip would ride on a sail just a few hundred atoms thick, a few meters wide.
segments.headline: A sail of light

segments.text: On Earth, a huge array of lasers would push the sails with light for a few minutes.
segments.headline: Pushed by lasers

segments.text: That could speed them up to about twenty percent of the speed of light.
They would fly past the Alpha Centauri stars, snap photos, and beam them home. The signal would take over four years to reach us.
segments.headline: Photos from another star

segments.text: The challenges are enormous: building the lasers, surviving dust impacts at that speed, sending a signal home. It may take decades.
segments.headline: Huge challenges

segments.text: Tomorrow, the fastest thing in the universe, and why nothing can beat it. Next stop: the speed of light. Follow, so you don't miss episode sixty-nine.
